description: The server's definition of the active-attention axis and of the §6 surface indicators, shared by both layers. Transcribed from packages/server/lib/data/repository/attention_dismissible_sql.dart and from the totals packages/server/test/data/repository/attention_active_attention_axis_pg_test.dart asserts against a real Postgres projection. Both layers read this file: client tests drive their expected totals from it instead of hand-building a number that looks right (U15R-c, overseer addition 1), and since U15R-d the server PG test that produces those numbers reads it too, so drift is caught from both ends. Since U18c the recorded per-case fields are §6's rules only; the three legacy totals are retired.

predicates._activeAttentionMeaning: activeOptional OR liveObligation — recorded as the composition the server source literally writes, so drift in either half is caught by its own entry

axisCases.name: seen but uncleared optional receipt still asks for attention
axisCases.note: reading is not clearing (D02): seen_at must not decide the dot

axisCases.name: unseen but cleared optional receipt no longer asks
a live obligation is active attention even when seen
axisCases.note: §6 splits what the retired `myWorkUnreadTotal` fused: the obligation is `my desk.count`, never `my desk.dot`. U18c retired that total; the two rules it fused are the two fields recorded here.

axisCases.name: a settled obligation stops being active attention

groupEventUnseenCount.definition: COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE activeOptional(child)) over primary-placement activity children
groupEventUnseenCount.note: eventUnseenCount is NOT a read count. A child that is seen but uncleared still counts; only cleared children drop out.

setO.description: dismissible outcome rows (inbox_item axis); excludes anything in eligible_pinned, i.e. an unanswered forward awaiting a decision (owner decision A)

unreadViewMembershipByItemKind.description: `is_active_attention` is not one expression. The stream union in attention_repository.dart gives each item_kind its own, and the client's `isInUnreadView` mirrors this table. R10: U15R-c applied the `receipt` rule to all four kinds, so a requestActivity card whose last optional child was cleared stayed on a list the server had already dropped it from.
unreadViewMembershipByItemKind.forward: false on the server list — an outcome row is dismissible and never served on `unread` (U15R-a/R1). The client mirror answers `seen_at IS NULL` instead: that is the forwardOutcomeTick (#601-a), the one unread tick on the row.

surfaceSummaryFields.description: What `AttentionRepository.surfaceSummary` returns, and which §6 rule each field is. §6 states four rules; before U15R-d the summary returned three fields and none of them was any of the four.
surfaceSummaryFields.myDeskDot: §6 `my desk.dot` — any owned Request has an uncleared optional event or uncleared outcome. Composed as activeOptional ∧ primaryPlacement on surface='myWork', OR a Set O row whose beacon is in `scope`. Live obligations are excluded: they are the number (D09).
surfaceSummaryFields.forYouDot: §6 `for you.dot` — Set R (dismissible optional receipts, wrapped in primaryPlacement) ∪ Set O (dismissible outcomes) ∪ eligible_pinned (the pending-forward zone) ∪ pending prompts.
surfaceSummaryFields.pendingPrompts: Written into the for-you dot as an explicit `OR FALSE` with a comment naming what it waits for. No classified prompt event has a row in any of the three sets yet (U09a); silent absence would be indistinguishable from a deleted predicate.
surfaceSummaryFields.forYouCount: Does not exist, at any layer. §6: `for you.count = never`. The absent field is what makes that structural rather than a convention a widget can break.
surfaceSummaryFields.myDeskCount: §6 `my desk.count` — the sum of `request.count` over owned Requests, i.e. live obligations. Composed as liveObligation ∧ primaryPlacement on surface='myWork'. Uncleared optional events are excluded: they are the dot, and D09 keeps dot and number independent. It was introduced as a NEW field rather than a re-scoping of the legacy `needsYouTotal`, which U18c has since retired. Since m0191 the surface leg drops nothing (a live obligation always names a Request, and any Request it names is in `scope`), so it is written because §6 states the rule that way, not to change the population.
surfaceSummaryFields.obligationsAlwaysNameARequest: m0191 (`notification_outbox__obligation_beacon_chk`, `CHECK (NOT requires_action OR beacon_id IS NOT NULL)`) makes a Request-less live obligation unstorable. Until U15R-e it was storable — m0115's `notification_outbox__beacon_policy_chk` demands a `beacon_id` only for the `beacon_content` / `beacon_tombstone` access policies — and `visibleWithSurface` labelled every beacon-less row `activity`, where §6 offers it neither a count nor a dot term. The constraint states the rule the producer already enforced (`AttentionPolicy.logicalTaskKey` throws `Live obligation requires a Request`) where nothing can route around it, and it validates on ADD so a legacy violating row aborts the migration rather than being skipped or repaired (legacy remediation is U18's). Pinned by the PG test 'U15R-e — a Request-less live obligation is rejected by notification_outbox__obligation_beacon_chk', asserted by constraint name.
surfaceSummaryFields.retiredTotals: U18c retired `activityUnreadTotal`, `myWorkUnreadTotal` and `needsYouTotal` from `AttentionSurfaceSummary` — server model, SQL, the GraphQL `AttentionSurfaceSummary` type, the client entity and its repository mapping. They kept their pre-U15R-d meaning (activeAttention per surface; every live obligation, unscoped) and their names said `unread`, which is the read axis §3 keeps separate; that contradiction produced two defects (U17a read one as History unread, U17b found a read-axis delta folded into another). The four §6 rules above are what the surfaces read and now all this summary returns. NOT retired, and not to be confused with these: `AttentionSummary.unreadTotal` and `AttentionSummary.needsYouTotal` on the *feed* summary, which are the counts behind the History `unread` and `needsYou` views — a read-axis surface §3 keeps alive.

forwardOutcomeTick.description: #601-a (owner decision): a forward row relabelled to an outcome moves up with ONE unread tick only when the relabel was not the viewer's own action. The `inbox:<beaconId>` row is synthetic, so the read marker lives on public.inbox_item (m0301): outcome_changed_at / outcome_changed_by are written by a trigger on every status change (actor = tentura.mutating_user_id, else the Hasura session user; a change with no known actor records nothing, except a move to status 3/4 — closed/deleted before the viewer answered — which only the Request's lifecycle or a forward cancel writes and which is recorded with a NULL actor), outcome_seen_at by markSeen. is_active_attention stays false: the tick is the read axis (seen_at), not the dot.
forwardOutcomeTick.unseen: seen_at IS NULL iff outcome_changed_by <> viewer AND outcome_changed_at > COALESCE(outcome_seen_at, '-infinity'); a NULL outcome_changed_by (an unattributed status 3/4 relabel) counts as not the viewer, so the SQL writes IS DISTINCT FROM. Otherwise seen_at = latest_forward_at as before.
forwardOutcomeTick.markSeen: markSeen with an inbox:<beaconId> id sets the viewer's own outcome_seen_at (only while a tick is pending); other users' rows and the row's position are untouched.

sql.unseen: ii.outcome_changed_at > COALESCE(ii.outcome_seen_at, '-infinity') AND ii.outcome_changed_by IS DISTINCT FROM

cases.name: relabelled by another user ticks and moves up
marking it seen clears the tick and keeps the position
the viewer's own relabel never ticks
a row whose outcome never changed stays at its entry
